rationale: The pull request addresses a bug where using --sort-reexports with multiline exports resulted in code mangling.
The issue describes an unhandled FileNotFoundError/OSError crash when encountering unreadable files or broken symlinks, which the pull request fixes by adding error handling.
The issue explicitly addresses regressions introduced by a previous pull request that broke existing tests and behavior.
The issue describes a bug where unindented comments inside indented blocks are improperly truncated and malformed by isort, causing syntax errors.
The pull request fixes a TypeError crash that occurs when passing glob patterns to the --src command line flag.
The issue describes an incorrect behavior where long lines with 'as' imports fail to receive a NOQA comment, and the pull request explicitly aims to fix this bug.
The issue describes an unrecoverable exception/crash when using the --interactive flag, and the pull request explicitly fixes this by treating EOF on stdin as 'quit'.
The issue describes a bug/regression where Zsh completion mishandles completion values containing colons, and the PR fixes this behavior.
The pull request fixes an inconsistency where setting `show_default` as a string is correctly displayed in the help text but ignored in the prompt, which constitutes incorrect behavior.
The pull request adds built-in PowerShell shell completion support, which introduces a brand new capability and extended support that was not present before in click v8.x.
The pull request extends the inference capability of the library to support new values for __name__, which corresponds to adding a new capability rather than fixing a bug or doing maintenance.

The issue describes an incorrect inference behavior depending on whether a module was previously imported, and the pull request aims to fix this bug by adjusting 'is_namespace()' to correctly handle 'ModuleSpec.loader'.
The issue describes an incorrect error being emitted for valid code involving properties with getters and setters, and the pull request aims to avoid these incorrect type errors.
The issue describes a crash and regression caused by an unsupported format string on a NoneType value, and the pull request aims to fix this error.
The issue and pull request describe fixing an OverflowError crash caused by large sequence multipliers.

The issue describes inconsistent inference behavior for JoinedStr depending on whether an unknown variable is declared, and the pull request explicitly targets improving this consistency as a bug fix.
The issue describes a traceback ending in an IndexError and a crash when analyzing incorrect code, which the pull request explicitly fixes.
The issue explicitly describes a crash caused by a RuntimeError ('dictionary changed size during iteration') when analyzing live objects, and the pull request title confirms it fixes this bug.
The issue describes an incorrect behavior where astroid imports and executes modules sharing names with standard library modules, and the pull request explicitly aims to fix this bug.
The issue and pull request title both describe fixing an IndexError crash when calling extract_node with invalid syntax, which represents fixing incorrect behavior.
The pull request fixes an unexpected AttributeError crash when processing a slice object used as a decorator on a six-decorated function.
The issue describes an AssertionError (crash) triggered by specific invalid code, and the pull request title explicitly states it fixes a crash.
The issue and pull request title explicitly state that .root() should return a module and aim to raise an error when it incorrectly returns a class instead, which is a bug fix for incorrect behavior.
The pull request fixes an unhandled TypeError crash caused by comparing an invalid dictionary literal.
The issue and pull request title both describe fixing a crash and ValueError caused by invalid input when inferring namedtuples.
The issue describes a crash caused by a MemoryError during parsing of deeply nested parentheses, and the pull request explicitly fixes this incorrect behavior.
The issue and pull request both address an IndexError crash caused by missing arguments when parsing specific types in astroid.
The task adds missing special attributes (__le__, __ge__) and moves dunders, extending the capabilities of ObjectModel and FunctionModel.
The issue describes an incorrect inference result where a default function argument value is treated as the only possible value, and the pull request is explicitly labeled as a bugfix.
The pull request fixes a TypeError crash that occurs when inferring random.sample code with uninferable sequence elements.
The issue describes incorrect behavior where super() inference returns the wrong instance type, and the pull request title explicitly states it fixes this incorrect type inference.
The pull request addresses a TypeError crash occurring during node cloning due to incorrect assumptions about ClassDef attributes.
The issue and pull request title both describe fixing a crash caused by an unexpected DuplicateBasesError during the dataclass transform, which is a bug fix.
The issue and pull request both address a MemoryError crash caused by inferring a formatted string with a large width value.
The issue describes a stack overflow (RecursionError/AstroidError) crash when parsing a module, and the pull request aims to enrich the resulting RecursionError with helpful advice.

The issue and pull request both explicitly state that a built-in function incorrectly exposes descriptor attributes and that it should be an inference error, which represents a fix for incorrect behavior.

The issue and pull request describe incorrect behavior where type inference for `str(const)` always returns an empty string `Const("")` instead of the correct inferred constant value, which constitutes a bug in the inference engine.
The pull request fixes an infinite recursion crash (RecursionError) occurring in _compute_mro() due to a circular MRO from name rebinding.
The issue describes incorrect code generation where necessary brackets are dropped, leading to syntax errors, and the pull request explicitly states it fixes this by wrapping expressions in parens.
The issue describes a traceback crash (AttributeError) when astroid encounters a specific fuzzed code snippet involving starred expressions, which represents incorrect behavior being fixed.
The issue describes an incorrect type inference error resulting in a false-positive lint failure, and the pull request explicitly aims to fix typing.self resolution during inheritance.
The pull request fixes an unexpected AttributeError crash occurring during dunder lookup when a non-class metaclass is used.
The issue describes an unhandled DuplicateBasesError crash when inferring an enum class with duplicate ancestors, and the pull request fixes this crash.
The issue describes a TypeError crash when using a functional Enum with non-string attributes, and the pull request explicitly aims to fix this crash.
The issue and pull request title describe fixing an AttributeError crash caused by an uninferable object during a getitem call, which falls under bug fixing.
The issue describes an unexpected traceback/crash when encountering an annotation-only __slots__ definition, and the pull request explicitly fixes this crash.
The pull request addresses an uncaught TokenError crash that occurs during fuzzing and provides a fix to avoid the exception.
The issue describes a crash caused by an unexpected keyword argument during inference, which the pull request fixes.
The issue describes a regression where Python stub files are no longer recognized and are shadowed by compiled modules, and the pull request title explicitly states it fixes this bug.
The issue describes an uncaught IndentationError crash when parsing certain code, and the pull request explicitly aims to fix it.
The issue describes a traceback crash (AttributeError) caused by an unsupported object type when calling qname(), and the pull request aims to fix this incorrect behavior.

The issue describes a false positive error (E1133 not-an-iterable) caused by incorrect handling of overloaded dunder methods, and the pull request title confirms it fixes this bug by ignoring typing.overload stubs.
The pull request title and issue description explicitly mention fixing incorrect behavior regarding regex pattern and match subscriptable inference that was previously xfailed.
The issue describes a TypeError crash occurring during inference when processing enums, and the pull request aims to fix crashes found by fuzzing.
The issue describes a traceback/crash (IndexError) triggered by invalid string formatting in an error message, and the pull request aims to fix this crash.
The issue describes an unexpected AttributeError crash when processing a specific dataclass structure, and the pull request aims to fix this crash.

The issue describes incorrect inference behavior where namedtuples created with rename=True keep invalid or duplicate names instead of properly renaming them like CPython, and the PR explicitly fixes this mismatch.
The issue describes a false positive caused by an incorrect fallback signature for `__new__` in the object model, which the pull request fixes.
The issue describes an IndexError crash during inference caused by specific function argument definitions, and the pull request explicitly fixes this crash.
The issue describes a hanging loop when parsing certain recursive or cyclic class structures, and the pull request is labeled as a bugfix for preventing infinite cycles during raw building.
The issue describes an unhandled OverflowError crash when inferring certain f-strings, and the pull request fixes this by catching the exception.
The pull request addresses a TypeError crash occurring during inference of random.sample() when processing certain elements, which fits the definition of a bug fix.
The issue and pull request title both describe fixing an unexpected TypeError crash that occurs during inference.
The issue and pull request title describe a TypeError crash occurring during inference, which is a classic bug fix.
The pull request fixes an unexpected crash caused by a ValueError during comparison inference with out-of-range bytes.
The issue describes a stack overflow/recursion crash during AST parsing, and the pull request aims to fix a RecursionError.

The issue describes incorrect behavior where augmented assignment on a list with a tuple value yields an uninferable result instead of the correct concatenation, and the pull request aims to fix this bug.
The issue describes an incorrect behavior where a source file remains open after a decoding error, and the pull request fixes this memory leak by properly closing the stream.
The issue describes broken AttributeError propagation when using cached_property with slots=True, which is incorrect behavior. The pull request fixes this specific mismatch in slotted classes.
The pull request adds a new validator called 'attrs.validators.or_', which introduces new capability to the library as requested in the issue.
The issue and pull request both address a syntax error crash that occurs when kw_only, defaults, and __attrs_pre_init__ are used together.
The issue describes an unexpected TypeError caused by unhashable sets when using filters with validators, and the pull request fixes this by transforming unhashable options to tuples.
The pull request adds a new capability and method (__attrs_init_subclass__) to the library, which was never supported before.
The issue describes a regression and AttributeError introduced in version 24.1.0 when assigning to fields with chained converters, which the pull request aims to fix.
The pull request restores basic functionality that was broken by a new CPython release, which is characteristic of fixing a regression/bug.
The issue describes a regression introduced in version 24.1.0 where combining optional and pipe converters causes a TypeError, which the pull request aims to fix.
The issue describes an error where validation checks are executed too early, preventing valid use cases involving custom field transformers, which constitutes incorrect behaviour.
The pull request improves an existing error message by including the name of the attribute, which is a minor enhancement to usability rather than fixing a bug or doing maintenance.
The pull request enables optional inner validators in deep_mapping, which adds new capabilities and extends support for a use case that previously required a cumbersome workaround.
The request asks for a new capability to override the class-level kw_only=True setting on individual attributes, which extends support for a configuration that was previously not possible.
The pull request adds new capability to the existing attrs.fields function by allowing it to accept an attrs class instance as input, extending its usability.
The pull request adds a new decorator for converters, extending the library's capabilities to match existing patterns like validator and default decorators.
The pull request fixes a ParseError where the parser incorrectly rejects valid TOML documents containing out-of-order arrays of tables.
The pull request addresses a security vulnerability where deeply nested TOML structures cause an uncontrolled recursion crash, fixing it by raising a controlled parse error instead.
The issue describes an incorrect behavior where emptying a dotted key incorrectly captures subsequent elements as its children, and the pull request explicitly aims to fix this bug.
